title: Scaling law for optimal excitation storage and superradiant release in waveguide QED systems
authors: Wei Chen, Kuan-Ting Lin, Guin-Dar Lin, Hsiang-Hua Jen
abstract: Driven-dissipative quantum emitters provide a powerful platform for controllable excitation storage and release, with promising applications in quantum batteries and quantum storage. Yet, transient excitation transfer in collective many-body systems is often obscured by the intricate interplay among coherent driving, dissipation, and correlation dynamics. Here, we uncover a scalable excitation-storage mechanism in two emitter ensembles coupled to a semi-infinite waveguide. A coherently driven ensemble acts as an effective excitation reservoir, while a second ensemble positioned near a dissipative node serves as a subradiant storage medium. Surprisingly, when the driven ensemble largely exceeds the storage ensemble in size, the transfer dynamics enters a nearly correlation-free regime, allowing the driven ensemble to behave effectively as a classical excitation source. This reveals a simple scaling law for optimal excitation transfer, under which the storage ensemble approaches near-complete population inversion as the driven ensemble size increases. Building on this mechanism, we propose a three-stage storage-and-release protocol enabling fast excitation storage and controllable photon emission. Our results demonstrate how coherent and dissipative collective interactions can be jointly harnessed for quantum energy storage and programmable nonequilibrium dynamics in waveguide QED platforms.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to control excitation storage and release in coupled emitter arrays embedded in waveguides. By analyzing the system's master equation, the authors derive a simple scaling law showing optimal transfer occurs when one ensemble is much larger than the other. This leads to a proposed three-stage protocol for programmable quantum energy management.
main_problem: The study aims to develop controllable mechanisms for storing and releasing quantum excitations using driven-dissipative emitter ensembles, overcoming challenges posed by complex interplay between driving, dissipation, and correlations.
main_result: The authors uncover a simple scaling law showing that optimal excitation transfer occurs when the size of the driven ensemble ($N_1$) greatly exceeds the storage ensemble ($N_2$), allowing for a three-stage protocol for energy management.
method: The analysis involves deriving and solving a Markovian master equation governing the collective spin dynamics, utilizing mean-field approximations in specific limits to simplify the many-body problem.
model_or_system: The system consists of two spatially separated ensembles of quantum emitters coupled to a semi-infinite waveguide. The dynamics are modeled by an effective Hamiltonian and master equation describing coherent driving, dissipation, and inter-ensemble coupling.

important_parameters: System size ratio ($N_1/N_2$), driving strength ($\Omega/\gamma$), and detuning ($\delta$). The limit $N_1 \gg N_2$ is crucial.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on identifying a nearly uncorrelated transfer regime when the driven ensemble size greatly exceeds the storage ensemble size, enabling a mean-field description.

paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model via a master equation, analyzes the dynamics by examining correlation regimes (dissipation-free vs. dissipative), derives scaling laws for optimal transfer, and concludes with a proposal for a three-stage storage-and-release protocol.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses controllable energy management in open quantum systems using waveguide QED, providing quantitative scaling laws that simplify complex many-body dynamics into predictable protocols for quantum memory and energy harvesting.
